claims.text: OffsetTracker's docstring claims it "Only commits offsets when all prior offsets are processed", but actual testing shows the gap-blocking only holds for one commit cycle: after the first commit advances last_committed, the next call to get_committable_offsets recomputes its starting point from min(remaining offsets) rather than last_committed+1, so a gap (e.g. offset 101 never entering the tracker) gets silently skipped and permanently lost on the second commit tick onward. The one test that pinned this invariant (test_handles_gaps) was deleted in this PR's final commit without explanation.

A queue_depth gauge fires once per processed message (message-processing frequency, an order of magnitude higher than this factory's other gauges which fire once per batch) inside OrderedQueueWorker.run's finally block.

decode_payload asserts not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload), but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy passes FilteredPayload messages to the decoder expecting None back - this causes AssertionError for filtered messages in thread-queue-parallel mode, which gets caught by broad except, logs spurious error, and silently discards the record by completing+committing the offset
Can the DB and Redis connection pools (and pgbouncer) handle 20 permanently-running worker threads each holding their own thread-local connections that are never explicitly recycled?

The worker transaction's name inherits a "monitors." prefix even though this module lives under remote_subscriptions/ with identifier "uptime" (producing misleading names like "monitors.uptime.worker_7"), and embeds worker_id in the name, which has no diagnostic value and multiplies the number of distinct transaction names by --max-workers.

Setting worker.shutdown = True before shutting down the queues means workers can exit without draining items still queued, leaving work unprocessed during shutdown and potentially preventing offsets from becoming committable for abandoned items during rebalances
pytestmark class attribute is a mutable list which triggers RUF012 - should be changed to immutable tuple (requires_kafka,)

Can the commit callable passed by arroyo to create_with_partitions safely be invoked from a strategy's own background thread, given every other strategy in this repo commits only from within arroyo's main loop (submit/poll), and this is the first to commit from a separate thread?
hash(group_key) % self.num_queues will raise ZeroDivisionError if num_queues is 0 - need to guard against num_queues <= 0 in __init__

Does the uptime-results topic actually experience offset gaps in practice (transaction control records, compaction), and is the consumer deployed with --stale-threshold-sec? Either would elevate F-003/F-004 from a theoretical correctness gap to an actively-triggered data-loss bug.
The magic number 50 for max_wait is used repeatedly throughout the tests. Consider extracting this as a named constant to improve maintainability.
Test assertion expects no commit after a processing error, but the queue worker completes offsets in `finally` and will still commit them.
Unused force parameter in track_commits functions in test_results_consumer.py - should rename to _force to satisfy Ruff linter

FixedQueuePool.shutdown() sets worker.shutdown = True for all workers before calling q.shutdown(immediate=False), creating a race where workers exit their while loop before draining remaining queued items, causing unnecessary reprocessing on restart

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit doesn't handle FilteredPayload messages: since the decoder asserts `not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload)`, every filtered message raises an AssertionError that gets caught by the broad except-Exception path and logged as an error, even though receiving a filtered message is normal operation.

The queue_depth gauge's tags only include `identifier`, without worker_id or queue_index, so all N workers overwrite the same metric time series — the resulting value represents neither any single queue nor a valid aggregate, and poll() already emits a meaningful aggregate (total_queued) separately.

test_different_groups_distributed asserts all 3 queues receive at least one of 20 distributed group keys (len(queue_indices) == 3), but since queue assignment uses hash(group_key) which is randomized per Python process (PYTHONHASHSEED not pinned anywhere in the repo), there is a ~0.09% chance one queue gets nothing, making this an intermittently flaky assertion.

OffsetTracker's four internal dicts (all_offsets, outstanding, last_committed, partition_locks) never remove entries for partitions that get revoked, so they grow unboundedly across rebalances; more importantly, if a partition is revoked and later reassigned with a lower starting offset, the stale last_committed value could permanently prevent that partition from ever computing a committable offset again.

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() shuts down the passed-in queue_pool, but the pool is created/stored on ResultsStrategyFactory and shared into each strategy instance - if create_with_partitions is called again (e.g., Kafka rebalance), the factory will reference a previously-shutdown pool and subsequent processing may break
strategy_processing_mode Literal type annotation in test base class not updated to include 'thread-queue-parallel', so subclasses using the new mode would be flagged by type checker

OrderedQueueWorker.run opens its own sentry transaction (op="queue_worker.process") wrapping each work item's processing, but ResultProcessor.__call__ — which it calls into — already opens its own transaction covering the same work, so the outer transaction adds a redundant layer with no coverage of anything beyond the inner one.
try-except-pass silently swallows all exceptions during cleanup when deleting test topic - should catch Kafka-specific exception and log the error instead
The test test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling has a docstring that doesn't match the test implementation.

The `FixedQueuePool` is owned by the factory but `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` shuts it down. After a Kafka rebalance, the next call to `create_with_partitions` will reuse the dead pool, silently dropping all messages. Either the strategy should not shut down the factory-owned pool in `close()`/`terminate()`, or the factory should recreate the pool in `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker`.

test_stats_reporting asserts stats["total_items"] > 0 immediately after submitting items, but this is racy: the 3 worker threads (already blocked on get() since setUp) process trivially fast compared to constructing WorkItems on the main thread, so the queue may already be drained by the time the assertion runs.
Unused timeout parameter in join method - should silence with _ = timeout to satisfy Ruff linter

FixedQueuePool.shutdown() sets each worker's shutdown flag to True before calling queue.shutdown(immediate=False), but since the worker loop condition checks `while not self.shutdown`, workers exit after at most one more item instead of draining the remaining queued items, defeating the immediate=False "drain" semantics that were deliberately chosen.

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/terminate()/join() all call queue_pool.shutdown(), but the FixedQueuePool is created once in the factory's __init__ and never rebuilt; since arroyo calls close() on the strategy at the start of every rebalance (as documented elsewhere in this repo for the spans flusher), the pool is irreversibly shut down after the first rebalance — every subsequent message submitted hits a dead queue, raises queue.ShutDown, gets caught by a broad except Exception, and the offset is still marked complete and committed — meaning the consumer looks healthy while silently dropping every message with no way to recover, even via restart, since offsets are already committed.

For Value (non-BrokerValue) messages — the shape used when DLQ machinery forwards already-processed offsets via DlqStaleMessagesStrategyFactoryWrapper — the exception-path offset bookkeeping only triggers when isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue), so those offsets are never recorded or committed at all, silently dropping them and creating exactly the kind of gap described in F-003.
Unused identifier parameter in result_processor function in test_queue_consumer.py - should rename to _identifier to satisfy Ruff linter

The seven new thread-queue-parallel unit tests were placed inside ProcessResultSerialTest, whose strategy_processing_mode is declared "serial" (and whose Literal type doesn't even include the new mode), so the class name and its declared processing mode now misrepresent what several of its test methods actually exercise.

wait_until_empty only checks qsize() which counts items in queue, but workers dequeue items before processing - queue can read as empty while workers are still executing, causing shutdown path to proceed before in-flight items finish and potentially skip complete_offset calls leaving offsets uncommitted

WorkItem.message stores the full original Kafka Message (including undecoded payload bytes) even though nothing in the codebase ever reads work_item.message — offset tracking uses the separate partition/offset fields — so every queued item unnecessarily doubles its memory footprint, compounding the unbounded-queue risk from F-002.

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() calls self.queue_pool.shutdown() which permanently destroys all workers and queues in the shared FixedQueuePool, causing any Kafka partition rebalance to leave the new strategy referencing a dead pool where submitted messages will never be processed

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() joins/stops the commit thread before shutting down the queue pool, so any offsets that finish processing (or, combined with F-006, offsets still sitting in the drained queue) after the commit thread stops are never committed, causing avoidable duplicate processing on every deploy.

The queue.shutdown() method with 'immediate=False' parameter may not exist in the standard Python queue module. This could cause AttributeError at runtime. Verify the correct API or implement a custom shutdown mechanism.
Unused identifier parameter in track_calls function in test_results_consumer.py - should rename to _identifier to satisfy Ruff linter

The worker queues have no maxsize and submit() never raises MessageRejected, so there is no real backpressure mechanism despite the class docstring explicitly claiming "Natural backpressure when queues fill up"; without MessageRejected (the only mechanism arroyo has to slow down a consumer), any slowdown downstream (DB, Redis) or lag catch-up after a restart will let messages pile up unbounded in memory, eventually causing OOM.

complete_offset is called in finally block, so offsets will be considered processed even when result_processor raises an exception, leading to committing past failed items and dropping them - contradicts docstring guarantee 'Only commits offsets after successful processing'
